structure.name: introduction
structure.guidance: Welcome the candidate, briefly explain the interview structure and what to expect. Allow the candidate to ask initial questions.

structure.name: technical_deep_dive
structure.guidance: Engage the candidate in a discussion covering mandatory skills. Focus on their experience with Go, distributed systems, Redis, microservices, and system design. Probe for their ability to design scalable services and mentor junior engineers. Use scenario-based questions to assess problem-solving and trade-off analysis.

structure.name: candidate_questions
structure.guidance: Provide an opportunity for the candidate to ask questions about the role, team, or company.

structure.name: closing
structure.guidance: Thank the candidate for their time and explain the next steps in the interview process.

mandatory_skills.evidence_to_look_for: Demonstrated understanding of Go concurrency patterns, error handling, standard library usage, and performance considerations. Ability to discuss Go project structures and best practices.

Ability to discuss challenges and solutions in distributed environments (e.g., consistency, fault tolerance, consensus, data partitioning). Experience with common distributed system patterns and protocols.
Knowledge of Redis data structures, use cases (caching, pub/sub, queues), and operational considerations (persistence, high availability, scaling). Ability to explain trade-offs of using Redis.
Experience designing, building, and operating microservices. Understanding of inter-service communication, API design, service discovery, and deployment strategies in a microservices architecture.

Ability to decompose complex problems, propose scalable and resilient architectures, identify critical components, and discuss trade-offs (e.g., CAP theorem, consistency models, latency vs. throughput).
Examples of guiding junior team members, providing constructive feedback, fostering growth, and contributing to team knowledge sharing. Understanding of effective mentorship strategies.

focus_areas: Experience with Go in production environments
Usage of Redis for specific use cases
Design and implementation of microservices architectures
Mentorship or leadership roles in previous teams
sample_questions: Tell me about a challenging distributed system you worked on. What was your role and what were the key technical decisions?
Can you describe a project where you heavily utilized Redis? What were the performance considerations?
Walk me through a microservice architecture you designed. What were the biggest challenges you faced?
Describe a situation where you mentored a junior engineer. What was the outcome?
What was the most complex system design problem you've tackled? How did you approach it?
Tell me about a time you had to lead a technical initiative. What was your approach?
Describe a situation where you had to resolve a conflict within your team regarding a technical decision.
Give me an example of a time you failed on a project. What did you learn from it?
How do you approach mentoring a junior engineer who is struggling with a complex task?
Tell me about a time you had to adapt to a significant change in project requirements or technology.

red_flags: Cannot explain trade-offs of chosen technology
No evidence of testing or code review discipline
Cannot estimate scale or performance constraints
Lack of understanding of fundamental distributed system concepts (e.g., CAP theorem, consistency models)
Inability to articulate design choices or justify technical decisions for scalable services
No experience or interest in mentoring or guiding less experienced engineers
Overly prescriptive solutions without considering alternatives or context
green_flags: Explains why a decision was made, not just what
Mentions monitoring, observability, or rollback strategy
References concrete production incidents and learnings
Clearly articulates complex distributed system concepts and their practical implications
Demonstrates a strong grasp of Go idioms, best practices, and performance optimization techniques
Provides clear examples of successful mentorship and team development
Proactively identifies potential system bottlenecks and proposes solutions during design discussions

evaluation_criteria.name: communication
evaluation_criteria.description: Clarity, structure, and responsiveness of answers.

evaluation_criteria.name: problem_solving
evaluation_criteria.description: Approach to ambiguous problems, trade-off analysis, decomposition.

evaluation_criteria.name: technical_depth
evaluation_criteria.description: Accuracy, breadth, and depth in required skills.

evaluation_criteria.name: system_design
evaluation_criteria.description: Ability to design scalable, maintainable systems.

evaluation_criteria.name: code_quality
evaluation_criteria.description: Readability, testing, error handling, best practices.

dos: Ask open-ended questions first, then drill down
Let the candidate finish their thought before interrupting
Ask for specific examples from past projects
Keep track of time per phase
Challenge architectural decisions with scale or failure scenarios
Ask about speed vs quality trade-offs and ownership
donts: Do not answer the question for the candidate
Do not make assumptions about background from the resume
Do not spend more than 20% of time on any single topic
